summary: Secondary string-table lookup variant of the message-buffer copy pattern. Looks up a string via BinarySearchInStringTable against the secondary table pointer off_5CCBCC[0]. On match, copies the table string into the global message buffer byte_5EC4CC, null-terminating it if the source pointer is null. Then copies up to a2-1 bytes from the message buffer into the caller-supplied output buffer a1 via sub_587DD0, null-terminates the output at a2-1+a1, and returns 0.

operations.description: Cache the secondary table entry pointer: v2 = off_5CCBCC[0].
BinarySearchInStringTable(byte_5EC4C0, off_5CCBCC[0], byte_5EC4CC): search the secondary string table for a key; non-zero return means a match.
Only copy into the message buffer when the table search reports a match.
When v2 is non-null, strcpy(byte_5EC4CC, v2): copy the matched string into the global message buffer.
When v2 is null, clear the message buffer: byte_5EC4CC[0] = 0.
sub_587DD0(a1, byte_5EC4CC, a2 - 1): copy or concatenate the message buffer into the caller output buffer a1 up to a2-1 bytes.
Null-terminate the output buffer at a2-1+a1.
Return 0 unconditionally after filling the output buffer.

unresolved: Relationship to the primary lookup (function with the same shape using the off_5CCBC4 table pointer) is not established; the two share the key/table buffer globals and differ only in the table pointer global.
sub_587DD0 semantics (copy vs concatenate, length handling) are in the callee and not confirmed here.
